# State Class View (variant): Wildland fire operations (crew to supervisor) (local)

> **Not a classification basis / not a job analysis / not for RIF or rating decisions.**

> Task importance, time share, critical and needed-at-entry values are agent drafts (raterType llm, validationStatus draft, evidence S): assessment pending (job analysis). They are not job-analysis results and no human has reviewed them. Target levels are editorial design drafts. A credential gate is shown only when its issuer is verified with a cited source; the other gates are counted, not shown, until the issuer is verified (CR-CP-001 C7).

- **Role:** Wildland fire operations (crew to supervisor) (`emst:forest/ROL-KB8K99D`, P1); authority position (editorial): resource-manager
- **Generated:** pipelines/views/state_class_view.py@0.2.0, rule state-class-view@0.1.0 (registered rule, status active), as of 2026-10-23

## Mapped classes

No class is mapped in the pilot jurisdictions (TX, WA and PA (state), Lewis County WA (county environmental health), Philadelphia Water Department (municipal utility)). The role's targets below are what a jurisdiction would crosswalk its own class specification against.

## Competency targets by role level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)

- Suppress wildland fire safely with ground tactics and resources — entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Manage risk in uncontrolled field environments — entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Operate chainsaws and other power equipment safely in field conditions — entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Use and maintain hand tools safely for field work — entry L1, journey L2, senior L2, lead L2
- Navigate and travel safely in remote terrain with and without digital aids — entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Predict fire behaviour from fuels, weather and topography for operations and planning — entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Lead field crews and transfer field judgment to novices — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Communicate during field emergencies and report incidents — entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Provide first aid and emergency medical care in remote field settings — entry L1, journey L2, senior L2, lead L3
- Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings — entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Conduct prescribed fire from burn planning through ignition, holding and evaluation — entry L1, journey L2, senior L2, lead L3
- Assess tree risk and structural condition — entry L1, journey L1, senior L2, lead L2
- Drive and operate field vehicles safely on unpaved roads and off road — entry L1, journey L2, senior L2, lead L2
- Maintain and repair field equipment and vehicles — entry L1, journey L1, senior L1, lead L1
- Evaluate and certify others' task performance against position standards — senior L3, lead L3
- Stabilize burned areas after wildfire from field assessment of burn severity and values at risk — journey L1
- Communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty — senior L2, lead L2
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — entry L1, journey L1, senior L1, lead L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — entry L1, journey L1, senior L1, lead L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — entry L1, journey L1, senior L1, lead L1
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — entry L1, journey L1, senior L1, lead L1
- Coordinate environmental response operations within incident command — entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Supervise staff and volunteers in environmental work — senior L3, lead L4
